title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: The Directors of the Company, key management personnel of the Company and the Company Secretary from time to time, and any other person advised by the Company Secretary that they are a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Close family members of a Restricted Person, including but not limited to a spouse/partner and minor children, and any family trust or family company that the Restricted Person or their Associates may control or in which they may have an interest.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: 'Prohibited Period' is defined as all times outside the three open windows, and any other period the Board specifies from time to time; the Board may also decide any other period is an open trading period. Confidentiality of any Board-specified addition is not addressed. Within an open window, the relevant approver may still embargo dealing to manage insider trading risk or on Front Page Test grounds.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives clause. A put and call are 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities in the Company', which is within the 'deal' definition, so entry requires prior written clearance under the general regime, is assessed against the Front Page Test, and is unavailable while in possession of MNPI. The Policy does not distinguish vested from unvested holdings.
rules.evidence: deal or dealing in securities means buy, sell or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company or financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities in the Company.

rules.detail: There is no dedicated hedging provision anywhere in the Policy. A risk-limiting arrangement over the shares is only regulated as an ordinary 'dealing' (a financial product created in respect of securities) requiring the standard clearance process.
rules.evidence: deal or dealing in securities means buy, sell or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company or financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a financial product created in respect of securities (a 'dealing'), requiring standard clearance; it may also risk characterisation as prohibited short-term dealing (see clause 12, which cites forward contracts as an example of banned short-term dealing).
rules.evidence: deal or dealing in securities means buy, sell or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company or financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or referenced anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named or referenced anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but are a financial product created in respect of securities and so a 'dealing' requiring standard clearance; a CFD used for short-term/speculative purposes would additionally risk the clause 12 ban.
rules.evidence: deal or dealing in securities means buy, sell or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company or financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban (newly added December 2025) on being party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right, in specified circumstances, to dispose of the Restricted Person's shares. No vesting-state carve-out and no clearance or exemption route stated.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not be party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right in specified circumstances to dispose of shares in the Company held by or on behalf of the Restricted Person.

rules.detail: The ban is tied to the lender's contractual right to dispose of the pledged shares; general encumbrance without a lender self-help disposal right is not separately addressed, but any customary secured-lending enforcement right would fall within the clause 16 ban.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not be party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right in specified circumstances to dispose of shares in the Company held by or on behalf of the Restricted Person.

rules.detail: Only margin loan facilities carrying a lender disposal right are expressly banned; the clause is titled 'No margin loans' and framed around that specific structure, with no exemption authority.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not be party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right in specified circumstances to dispose of shares in the Company held by or on behalf of the Restricted Person.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on speculative or short-term dealing. On-market buying and selling within 6 months is one example; entering into 'other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)' is separately named, meaning forward-style derivatives risk being treated as inherently short-term regardless of tenor. Securities acquired on vesting under an equity incentive or share plan are excluded.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal in securities of the Company on a speculative or short term trading basis. Short term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

exemption_authority: During a Prohibited Period, the relevant approver (Nominated Director, Chair of the Board, or Company Secretary, per the section 9 table) has absolute discretion to grant written clearance to trade if satisfied exceptional circumstances exist (severe financial hardship, a court order or other legal requirement, or any other circumstance in the approver's discretion), provided the person holds no MNPI, and only after making reasonable enquiries. Approval may be made conditional or later revoked, may be refused without reasons, and a refusal must be kept confidential. Clause 16's margin loan ban has no exemption route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the approver does not consider that the dealing would satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar and loan structure can be refused clearance on a subjective reputational test, with no right to reasons if refused.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly cites forward contracts as an example of banned 'short term dealing'; a bank collar structured via forward-type OTC derivatives risks being characterised as prohibited short-term or speculative dealing regardless of its stated tenor.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not be party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right in specified circumstances to dispose of shares in the Company held by or on behalf of the Restricted Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This newly added clause (December 2025) targets the lender's contractual right to dispose of pledged shares; a standard bank loan secured on the collared shares with customary enforcement/margin-call rights would squarely breach it, with no exemption or clearance route stated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Restricted Person is not entitled to receive any reasons for why the dealing request has been denied. If approval is denied, the Restricted Person must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A refused clearance for the collar's derivative leg comes with no explanation and cannot be discussed, complicating any attempt to restructure and reapply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: They must not structure arrangements or procure third parties to deal in securities of the Company to circumvent the operation of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an associate, intermediary or synthetic wrapper to avoid the margin loan ban or clearance requirement is expressly prohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibited Period means all times outside of the periods mentioned in paragraph 7.1 ... In order to obtain prior written clearance ... in accordance with sections 7.1 or 7.2 of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Internal cross-references still point to superseded section numbers (7.1/7.2) rather than the current sections 9 and 10, an artefact of the December 2025 renumbering when clause 16 was inserted; the intended meaning is clear from context but the drafting is imprecise.

summary: A funded collar faces a clear prohibition on its financing leg and material risk on its derivative legs under this policy. Clause 16, added in December 2025, bans a Restricted Person from being party to any margin loan facility that gives the lender the right, in specified circumstances, to dispose of the pledged shares — language that squarely captures a standard bank loan secured on the collared shares with customary enforcement rights, and no exemption or clearance route is provided. The put and call legs are not addressed by any dedicated hedging or derivatives clause; as 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities', they are ordinary 'dealings' requiring prior written clearance from the Nominated Director, Chair of the Board or Company Secretary (as applicable), assessed against a subjective Front Page Test and refusable without reasons, and are further complicated by clause 12's ban on short-term dealing, which expressly cites forward contracts as an example of prohibited short-term dealing irrespective of the six-month on-market benchmark. Clearance is generally available as a matter of course within six-week windows following results releases, a prospectus issue or the AGM, and otherwise only in exceptional circumstances (severe hardship, court order, or the approver's discretion); the Policy does not distinguish vested from unvested holdings. Overall, the loan leg is prohibited outright and the derivative legs face real approval and short-term-dealing risk, making a fully funded collar difficult to implement as structured.
